title: BlackSky Acquires Data Science Firm EpochGeo
html:
BlackSky ($BKSY) announced its acquisition of geospatial data science firm EpochGeo yesterday, which will merge EpochGeo’s AI/ML capabilities with BlackSky’s existing constellation and analytics tools.

There’s no shortage of imagery flowing into defense customers’ hands. But, to make it usable for quick decision-making, companies are working to shift from capturing pixels to automatically fusing electronic signals with overhead photos in real time.

“BlackSky’s satellites and AI already show customers what is happening at the places that matter most to them,” BlackSky CEO and president Brian O’Toole told Payload via email. “EpochGeo adds the ability to tell them where they should be taking a closer look.”

The target: Founded in 2018, EpochGeo builds software that fuses RF signals, publicly available data, and satellite imagery into real-time intelligence.

“By bringing imagery, signals and other data sources like ship and aircraft tracking into one analytical environment, BlackSky can now collect, fuse and analyze that data as a single provider,” O’Toole said.

For BlackSky, the deal connects two critical halves of the intelligence loop:

  • Integrating EpochGeo’s AI/ML software gives BlackSky’s platform a way to layer RF signals over its high-resolution Gen-3 optical imagery.
  • The acquisition also potentially adds dozens of already cleared engineers to the workforce—a valuable commodity in the industry-wide battle for talent.

EpochGeo will also carry over active contracts with US and international defense contractors and government agencies. BlackSky plans on continuing to support EpochGeo’s existing customer contracts alongside the integration.

“Just as important, EpochGeo’s data fusion and AI experience supporting US combatant commands and international ministries of defense is the kind of work our largest customers are asking for,” O’Toole said. “It’s a strong fit for our international government business.”

The balance sheet: BlackSky released its Q3 results Nov. 5, with a record revenue of $42.8M—up 118% YoY—and record space-based intelligence and AI services revenue of $32.7M. The company also raised its full-year revenue guidance for the second time—estimating $140M-$150M for 2026.

BlackSky attributed the growth to demand for its Gen-3 satellites—with five sats in orbit and a sixth targeting launch NET Dec. 30.
summary: BlackSky ($BKSY) announced its acquisition of geospatial data science firm EpochGeo yesterday, which will merge EpochGeo’s AI/ML capabilities with BlackSky’s existing constellation and analytics tools.
